claim.qualifier: EPA combined unloaded range. Ford simultaneously advertises 10,000 lb tow capacity for Extended Range trim. The two figures appear together in marketing without disclosure that towing collapses range.
claim.verbatim_quote: EPA Range: 320 miles … Up to 10,000 pounds towing rating with Extended Range battery

sources.name: Ford F-150 Lightning marketing materials (via Consumer Reports overview)

reality.qualifier: Range while towing a 6,000–7,200 lb trailer at highway speed. MotorTrend instrumented testing measured 90–115 mi across three trailer weights. Owner-reported real-world: 0.8 mi/kWh towing 6,000 lb Airstream vs 1.5–1.8 mi/kWh solo (~50% loss).
reality.verbatim_quote: With the smallest and lightest trailer, we measured a range of just 115 miles. That figure fell to 100 miles with the middleweight camper and sank to a mere 90 miles with the 7,218-pound Grand Design trailer.

sources.name: MotorTrend / Automobile — F-150 Lightning towing test (3 trailer weights)
F-150 Lightning Forum / Electrek — owner real-world tow test, 23-foot Airstream ~6,000 lb
Recharged — Ford F-150 Lightning Towing Review & Real-World Range

narrative_one_liner: Ford pairs '10,000 lb tow capacity' with '320 mi range'; real towing range with mid-size trailer is ~100 mi (–69%).
narrative: Ford advertises 320 mi EPA range and 10,000 lb tow capacity as separate headline numbers. Independent testing shows that towing a typical 6,000–7,200 lb trailer at highway speeds drops range to roughly 90–150 miles — a 50–70% reduction. MotorTrend, Recharged, and owner forum tests converge on this. The truck does internally re-estimate range when a trailer profile is entered, but the marketing positions both numbers as if a buyer can plan towing trips around the EPA figure.
methodology_notes: Three independent sources converge: MotorTrend instrumented multi-trailer tests; Recharged synthesis of owner data; Electrek covering an owner forum-reported real-world test. N≥3 independent measurements.
caveats: The earliest Tier-2 measurement (MotorTrend) is from 2022 on a 2022 Platinum trim; powertrain unchanged through 2024 ER per EPA filings.

Severity 'critical' reflects safety angle: a buyer who plans a 200-mi towing leg based on the EPA number and discovers ~100 mi reality could be stranded with a heavy trailer. This is the only Phase 0 record where stranding risk is the harm vector.
Lightning's truck UI does internally reduce range estimate when a trailer profile is entered, partially mitigating in-vehicle deception (if not marketing-page deception).
alternative_explanations: Trailer aerodynamics dominate efficiency; results vary widely with trailer shape. We use a typical mid-size trailer as the canonical case.
Speed dramatically affects towing range; the 50% number assumes ~65–70 mph. Higher speeds collapse further.
